questions.question: After the DMA controller finishes a transfer, what does it do with the HOLD signal?

options.A: It asserts HOLD to keep the processor halted
options.B: It toggles HOLD to request another transfer
options.C: It turns off HOLD, allowing the processor to regain bus control
options.D: It leaves HOLD unchanged until the processor resets

questions.explanation:
The context states that once the DMA controller is done, it turns off the HOLD signal and the microprocessor takes back control of the buses. [Page 80]  

---

questions.question: Which buses does the DMA controller temporarily borrow from the microprocessor during a transfer?

options.D: The address bus, data bus, and control bus

questions.explanation:
The DMA controller temporarily borrows the address bus, data bus, and control bus to move data directly between an I/O port and memory. [Page 80]  

---

questions.question: What is the purpose of the HOLD signal in a microprocessor‑based DMA system?

options.A: To acknowledge completion of a DMA transfer
options.B: To request the processor to release the buses after the current bus cycle
options.C: To reset the DMA controller after each transfer
options.D: To indicate a data parity error on the bus

questions.explanation:
HOLD is described as a bus request signal that asks the microprocessor to release control of the buses after the current bus cycle. [Page 80]  

---

questions.question: In a DMA read transfer, the direction of data flow is:

options.D: Between two memory locations without using the CPU

questions.explanation:
The context defines a read transfer as data moving from memory to an I/O device. [Page 82]  

---

questions.question: Which DMA operation generates addresses without causing actual memory or I/O control signals?
questions.explanation:
Verification operations generate the DMA addresses but do not generate DMA memory and I/O control signals. [Page 82]  

---

questions.question: What is the maximum amount of data a single DMA channel can be programmed to transfer?
questions.explanation:
Each channel can independently program to transfer up to 64 KB of data. [Page 82]  

---

questions.question: Which functional block of the 8257 DMA controller is responsible for determining which channel gets the bus when more than one request is pending?
questions.explanation:
The functional blocks listed include a priority resolver, which resolves competing channel requests. [Page 82]  

---

questions.question: Which of the following statements about DMA controller interfaces is correct?

options.A: A DMA controller can only be connected to a single I/O interface.
options.B: DMA controllers are never designed to handle multiple interfaces.
options.C: Some DMA controllers are associated with a single interface, but many are designed for multiple interfaces.
options.D: All DMA controllers must have exactly two interfaces.

questions.explanation:
The text notes that sometimes a DMA controller is associated with a single interface, but they are often designed to accommodate more than one interface. [Page 80]  

---

questions.question: Which register keeps track of how many bytes or words have been transferred during a DMA operation?
questions.explanation:
The count register is used to count the number of byte or word transferred by DMA. [Page 82]  

---

questions.question: When the DMA controller is active, what happens to the microprocessor’s ability to execute instructions?

options.B: It is temporarily disabled while the DMA borrows the buses.
options.C: It enters a low‑power sleep mode but can still access registers.
options.D: It can only execute branch instructions.

questions.explanation: The DMA technique provides direct access to memory while the microprocessor is temporarily disabled, as the DMA borrows the buses. [Page 80]
